title: yaks core keyword vocabulary
description: The keywords the yaks meta-model adds to JSON Schema 2020-12 to describe a component vocabulary. Native JSON Schema still carries type, format, enum, const, default, description, examples, $ref/$defs; these keywords add what a component table needs on top. Native keywords reach the table too: `type: integer` stores with integer affinity, a component's `required` list is NOT NULL, `default` is the column default (`{"now": true}` for the clock), and `enum` is a check. `examples` is native and subsumes the old `well` concept: a text field's completion draws from its examples union the property's own live distinct values.
$comment: A vocabulary declaration in the JSON Schema sense: a URI that names this keyword set, plus the schema of each keyword. A vocabulary document declares it under $vocabulary.

component.description: true = this $defs entry declares a component: an object schema whose `properties` are the component's properties. Required — an entry marked neither this nor `tool` is an ordinary reusable subschema, and the loader creates no table for it.

extends.description: true = this component entry adds its properties to a component another document declares, instead of declaring one of its own. The spine is what it is for: `entity` is declared once, and a plugin that keeps a value beside every entity adds its property here. An extension carries properties and nothing else — kind, prefix, indexes and wire belong to the document that declares the component.

tool.description: true = this $defs entry declares a tool: one named operation an agent can ask the graph to perform. The implementation is a function the module exports, looked up by the entry name (or noun_verb); the declaration is the part that is sent to clients.

rule.description: true = this $defs entry declares a rule: a query the graph runs over every batch of changes, and nothing else. There is no implementation anywhere — the `match` query is the rule, and the components its `+` patterns name are what it writes.

match.description: A rule's query: one or more ordinary query patterns separated by `;`, one per entity, joined by the variables they share. `$call .call, results=; +result.call=$call`.

noun.description: A tool's resource word, one lowercase word — what it acts on. Declared beside a `verb` it is half of a two-word command a CLI accepts in either order (`session list`, `list session`); declared alone it is the whole command name, both on the command line and in an MCP request (`history`).

verb.description: A tool's operation word, one lowercase word — what it does. Declared beside a `noun` it is the other half of the two-word command; declared alone it is the whole command name, both on the command line and in an MCP request (`land`).

input.description: A tool's arguments: one JSON Schema per named argument, the same shape a component's `properties` takes. The entry's `required` list names the arguments a call must supply.

ref.description: The entity kind a string property references, e.g. "project" or "entity" (any entity). Makes the property a reference that stores the target's internal id.

death.description: What the reaper does to this reference when its target entity dies.

sync.description: Who is told about a write to this component. "server" (the default) sends it to the server, which owns it and fans it out to subscribers; "none" keeps it on the writing node; "peers" sends it to the server, which relays it to subscribers without storing it.

durable.description: How long a value of this component lives, asked of whoever owns it. "forever" (the default) is storage — SQLite and the journal on a server, the vault in a client. "connection" is memory keyed by the writer's connection, swept when that connection closes. A duration ("5s", "2m") is that plus a timer, restarted on each write.

pace.description: How often a relayed ("sync": "peers") value of this component is sent, as a duration ("100ms"). The writer's own graph takes every write at once; the peers hear the latest value at most once a pace, the last one always, and a clear at once. Absent, every write is sent as it is made.

computed.description: true = this property is derived, never stored: no column holds it, nobody writes it, a reader still sees it (a query-only rank, an aggregate, a status read off marks). Default false — a property nobody declares so is stored.

reads.description: On a computed property: the components on other entities its value is read from, so a change to an entity wearing one of them can move it. [] = the entity's own components alone. A computed property that declares none may read anything, and every change can move it.

stamped.description: true = the server owns this property: clients can read it, never write it.

search.description: On a property, true = this text property is full-text indexed: a bare word in a query matches it, and a hit is ranked by it. A property nobody declares is stored and readable but never searched. On a component, the text its entities are found by, as `comp.prop` names of one other component's properties: `entry` says ["content.body"], so a transcript entry is found by what it says, and other entities carrying `content` are not.

kind.description: true = this component names a display kind (feeds kindOf / kindOrder).

before.description: Kind names this kind sorts before. kindOrder is alphabetical, topologically refined by these constraints. On a rule it names the rules this one runs before, so order among rules touching one entity is declared rather than registration-incidental.

wire.description: false = clients can read this component but never write it (the spine component, `entity`). Default true.

bare.description: false = this property (or every property of this component) never claims its bare filter name; it is reached qualified only (.comp.prop). Use it for a property that should only be queried explicitly — a large log partition, or a name another component already claims.

aliases.description: Input forms that resolve to an enum member; output always uses the canonical member.

unique.description: A uniqueness constraint, which is what decides a race between two writers. On a property, true = no two rows of the component may share the value. On a component, the composite uniques as property lists: [["space", "slug"]], or {"props": ["key"], "present": ["key"]} for a unique over the rows that hold the key (a partial index).

identity.description: What the entity's own id is derived from. On a property, true = this component's entities are identified by this value: the eid is sha256("<component>|<value>") formatted as a UUID, so writing the same value twice writes one entity and uniqueness is a property of the id rather than the outcome of a race. On a component, the property list a composite identity spans, in derivation order: ["space", "slug"]. One tuple, never a list of them — an entity has one id.

index.description: An index to read by, with no uniqueness constraint. On a property, true = index it. Stored references are always indexed: true is redundant and false does not opt out. On a component, the composite indexes as property lists: [["app", "version"]], or {"props": [...], "present": [...]} for a partial index over the rows that hold those properties.
